いってらっしゃい.gloss: have a good day; see you later

meanings.en: have a good day; take care (said to someone leaving)
meanings.note: Standard greeting said by those staying behind when someone leaves home.

examples.text: いってらっしゃい、気をつけてね。
examples.trans: Have a good day, take care.

examples.text: いってらっしゃい、早く帰ってね。
examples.trans: See you later, come home early.

meanings.note: Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Conjunction expressing annoyance or reproach toward someone's behavior.

examples.text: 知らないくせに偉そうに言うな。
examples.trans: Don't talk big even though you don't know.

examples.text: 暇なくせに手伝ってくれない。
examples.trans: Even though he's free, he won't help.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.en: anyway; after all; in any case
meanings.note: Adverb expressing resignation, skepticism, or a foregone conclusion.

examples.text: どうせ今日も遅くなるよ。
examples.trans: I'll end up being late today anyway.

examples.text: どうせ誰も信じてくれない。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Loanword from English 'game'.

examples.text: 新しいゲームを買った。

meanings.en: slack off; cut corners; play hooky
meanings.note: Colloquial godan verb from French 'sabotage'.

examples.text: 仕事をサボってはいけません。
examples.trans: You must not slack off at work.

examples.text: 授業をサボって映画を見た。
examples.trans: I skipped class and watched a movie.

meanings.note: Affectionate family word used by children and spouses at home.

examples.text: パパは料理が上手です。
日曜日はパパと出かけます。
examples.trans: On Sundays I go out with Dad.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.note: Small-denomination coins.

examples.text: ポケットに小銭が入っています。
examples.trans: There is loose change in my pocket.
I don't have enough loose change.

meanings.en: go home; leave and go back
meanings.note: Repeated past form 帰った、帰った! is an idiomatic shooing command ('off you go, go on home!').
Adverbial form 早く urges someone to hurry up.

examples.trans: I woke up early in the morning.

meanings.note: Working beyond regular business hours; pairs with する.

examples.text: 今日は残業があります。
毎日残業で疲れています。
examples.trans: I'm tired from working overtime every day.

行ってくる.gloss: I'm heading out; I'll be back

meanings.en: I'm heading out; I'll go and come back
meanings.note: Set phrase said when leaving home or the office.

examples.text: ちょっとコンビニに行ってくる。
examples.trans: I'm going to run to the convenience store.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective describing either late timing or slow speed.

examples.text: 今日は帰りが遅いです。
この電車は少し遅いですね。
examples.trans: This train is a little slow, isn't it?

meanings.note: Te-form 遊んで before きていい asks permission to go play and come back.

examples.trans: I am going outside to play.

examples.text: 子供たちが庭で遊んでいます。
examples.trans: Children are playing in the yard.

meanings.note: 頑張ります! is the classic cheerful commitment when starting a job or task.

examples.trans: I will do my best today too.
Do your best on the exam!
